title: Refactor export schema for stable proration traceability
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description:
Problem:
We observe recurring reconciliation drift between our internal usage ledger and Stripe/NetSuite invoice lines in scenarios where customers: intermittent quota changes mid-billing-cycle, multiple plan/component swaps, or transient rate-limit credit backfills. Current export schema flattens proration context into free-form text and splits adjustments across multiple lines without a deterministic linkage token, making downstream matching and automated corrections error-prone.

Goal:
Refactor the billing export schema to include deterministic proration traceability fields so that every exported invoice line/event includes: a stable proration_id, original_usage_anchor timestamps, contributing charge components, and an explicit reason code (e.g., MIDCYCLE_PLAN_SWAP, LATE_USAGE_BACKFILL, THROTTLE_CREDIT). This enables deterministic reconciliation, idempotent replays, and simpler heuristics for NetSuite line merging.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
1) Exports to Stripe/NetSuite include the new top-level fields: proration_id, anchor_window_start, anchor_window_end, contributor_tags (comma-separated), and proration_reason_code.
2) Existing consumers (billing export runner, invoice-generator, and export sanity checks) remain backward-compatible: when older systems consume the new fields they should ignore unknown fields; when new consumers read old exports they must reconstruct nominal proration_id using a stable hashing fallback.
3) Reconciler testbench verifies that previously flaky cases (plan-swap at 23:59 UTC, late rate-limit backfill, and multi-currency swap) now yield deterministic line matches in >99.99% of simulated runs.
4) Deployment includes a migration plan and an offline data repair tool to emit proration_ids for historical exports up to 90 days.

Proposed approach:
- Schema change: introduce a v2 export payload for invoice_line objects with explicit fields (all string typed for consumer stability).
- Generation: billing exporter will calculate proration_id := sha256(customer_id + billing_period_start + change_event_seq) truncated to 16 hex chars; include contributor_tags like "quota_adjust,rate_limit_credit,plan_swap".
- Export writer: add version header (export_schema_version=v2) and a compatibility shim that writes a fallback "legacy_proration_hint" text blob for consumers that haven't migrated.
- Reconciler: update matching logic to prefer proration_id exact matches, then fall back to (customer, amount, anchor_window_start/end) with stricter heuristics.
- Migration: one-off job to backfill historical exports (90-day window) writing new export objects to a separate archive bucket and running reconciliation simulation to assert equivalence.

Data validation & monitoring:
- Add export checksum and proration_id uniqueness validation.
- Dashboard: new Grafana panel in billing-recon showing percent of invoice_lines with proration_id present, and reconciliation success rate pre/post change.
- Alerts: fire if >0.1% of daily invoices for customers with mid-cycle events lack proration_id after rollout.

Rollout plan:
1) Beta export_schema_version=v2 behind a feature flag for 10% of accounts (no change to invoice generation).
2) Monitor for seven days; run reconciler in "dry-run" mode comparing v1 vs v2 matching rates.
3) Expand to 50% and then 100% if metrics stable; flip reconciler to prefer proration_id only after 50% completion.
4) Run backfill job for last 90 days once stable and reconcile results to ensure no invoice deltas.

Notes on edge cases:
- Multi-currency plan swaps: proration_id must include canonical pricing_key to ensure hash stability across currency conversions.
- Retry storms: ensure proration_id is stable across retry attempts by including change_event_seq that is deduplicated at source.
- Very small adjustments (< $0.01 rounding): tag contributor_tags with "rounding" and allow downstream merge into parent line per NetSuite mapping rules.
